children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts continued their downward slide at midday Friday, touching fresh four-month lows.
January canola was down C$5.90 at C$747.30 per metric ton at mid-session. The contract fell below its 200-day moving average on Thursday, likely encouraging additional speculative selling.
"We're definitely in bearish territory for the charts on canola," said an analyst.
Losses in Chicago soyoil accounted for some spillover selling pressure. European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil were also weaker, with palm oil at its lowest levels in eight months.

Weakness in the Canadian dollar, which was down by roughly half a cent relative to its U.S. counterpart, was supportive as the softer currency underpins crush margins and makes exports more attractive to international buyers.
An estimated 40,400 canola contracts traded as of 11:20 a.m. EST.
